body.statement:
For fixed \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(M_1>0\), and \(M_2>M_1^2\), there is a finite constant \(A_{\mathrm{ph}}\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\), such that, simultaneously for every \(C\ge1\), every \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\), and every integer \(0\le k\le\lfloor T/2\rfloor\),
\[
 E_M\!\left[(\widehat\theta_k-\theta(K,e))^2\right]
 \le 4M_1^2q_C^2\alpha^{2k}
       +\frac{A_{\mathrm{ph}}}{T}\{1+L^k\}.
\]
The bound is uniform in \(C\) and in all finite alphabet cardinalities.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(C\ge1\) and a member \(M\in\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\).  Write
\[
 m(s,a):=E_K[Y_t\mid S_t=s,A_t=a].
\]
The conditional-moment envelope in \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}reward}\) gives \(|m(s,a)|\le M_1\), \(E_K[Y_t^2\mid S_t=s,A_t=a]\le M_2\), and hence \(|g_e(s)|\le M_1\).  These bounds are well defined for every \((s,a)\) because \(K(\cdot\mid s,a)\) is a probability kernel by \(\mathrm{ass{:}pomdp\text{-}kernel}\).

We first retain the stationary-overlap radius in the usual partial-history bias calculation.  If \(C>1\), then
\[
 \nu_C:=\frac{Cd_b-d_e}{C-1}
\]
is a probability law: it is nonnegative by \(\mathrm{ass{:}latent\text{-}stationary\text{-}overlap}\), and its total mass is \((C-1)/(C-1)=1\).  Since \(q_C=(C-1)/C\),
\[
 d_b-d_e=q_C(\nu_C-d_e),
 \qquad
 \|d_b-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le q_C. \tag{1}
\]
If \(C=1\), the pointwise inequalities \(d_e(s)\le d_b(s)\), together with the fact that both laws sum to one on the finite space \(\mathcal S\), imply \(d_e=d_b\), so (1) also holds because \(q_1=0\).

On every behavior-supported action cell, \(0\le\rho_t\le L\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}policy\text{-}overlap}\); cells outside behavior support have target probability zero and use the stipulated zero convention.  Repeated conditional expectation under \(\mathrm{ass{:}sequential\text{-}ignorability}\) therefore changes the last \(k+1\) action laws from \(b\) to \(e\).  The Markov factorization in \(\mathrm{ass{:}pomdp\text{-}kernel}\) then gives
\[
 E_M[Z_t(k)]=d_bP_e^kg_e. \tag{2}
\]
Since \(d_eP_e^k=d_e\), iteration of \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}contraction}\), followed by (1), yields
\[
 \|d_bP_e^k-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\alpha^k\|d_b-d_e\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le q_C\alpha^k. \tag{3}
\]
Integration of a function bounded in absolute value by \(M_1\) changes by at most \(2M_1\) times total variation.  Thus (2), (3), and \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}value}\) imply
\[
 \left|E_M[Z_t(k)]-\theta(K,e)\right|
 \le2M_1q_C\alpha^k. \tag{4}
\]

We next record the moment calculation, including the absence of a history-length multiplier.  The elementary inequality \(\rho_t^2\le L\rho_t\), followed successively by conditional expectation over the actions, gives
\[
 E_M[Z_t(k)^2]\le M_2L^{k+1}. \tag{5}
\]
For \(1\le h\le k\), the two likelihood-ratio products in \(Z_t(k)Z_{t+h}(k)\) overlap at \(k+1-h\) action times.  At each overlap use \(\rho^2\le L\rho\); at each remaining action use likelihood-ratio cancellation.  Conditional expectation of the two rewards along the resulting Markov path produces two conditional reward means, each bounded by \(M_1\).  Since the two score means agree by behavior stationarity from \(\mathrm{ass{:}stationary\text{-}start}\), subtracting their squared common mean cannot increase the covariance upper bound.  Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_M\{Z_t(k),Z_{t+h}(k)\}
 \le M_1^2L^{k+1-h},
 \qquad 1\le h\le k. \tag{6}
\]
For \(h\ge k+1\), the two action windows do not overlap.  The same conditional-expectation calculation expresses the cross moment as the integral of the product of two functions bounded by \(M_1\), with the intervening state law propagated for \(h-k-1\) behavior steps and the future reward regression propagated for \(k\) target steps.  Applying the total-variation contraction first to the behavior segment and then to the target segment gives
\[
 \left|\operatorname{Cov}_M\{Z_t(k),Z_{t+h}(k)\}\right|
 \le2M_1^2\alpha^{h-1},
 \qquad h\ge k+1. \tag{7}
\]
Equations (5)--(7) use only finite likelihood-ratio sums and the two contractions.  They therefore hold for every finite action alphabet, and their constants contain no alphabet cardinality.

Let \(N:=T-k\).  Stationarity and the finite-sum variance identity give
\[
 \begin{split}
 \operatorname{Var}_M\!\left(N^{-1}\sum_{t=k+1}^TZ_t(k)\right)
 &\le \frac1N\left\{M_2L^{k+1}
      +2M_1^2\sum_{h=1}^kL^{k+1-h}
      +4M_1^2\sum_{h=k+1}^{\infty}\alpha^{h-1}\right\}\\
 &\le \frac1N\left\{
      \left(M_2L+\frac{2M_1^2L}{L-1}\right)L^k
      +\frac{4M_1^2}{1-\alpha}\right\}.
 \end{split}\tag{8}
\]
The two series in (8) are geometric; in particular, no factor \(k\) occurs.  When \(k\le T/2\), \(N^{-1}\le2T^{-1}\).  Define
\[
 A_{\mathrm{ph}}:=2\left\{M_2L+\frac{2M_1^2L}{L-1}
                  +\frac{4M_1^2}{1-\alpha}\right\}<\infty. \tag{9}
\]
The strict inequalities \(L>1\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), which follow from \(\zeta>0\) and \(t_0>0\), justify both divisions in (9).  Combining the squared bias from (4) with (8)--(9) proves the asserted bound for the unclipped average.  Finally, the moment envelope gives \(\theta(K,e)\in[-M_1,M_1]\), so projection onto this interval cannot increase squared distance to \(\theta(K,e)\).  This proves the same bound for \(\widehat\theta_k\).
